objective: Remote-only DevOps repair task. qjns and uiap are online but report disk free = 0 in Control Plane and must be repaired before implementation/MIMO/RAG work. From a server command/control node, perform read-only triage first, classify disk usage, then execute only minimal safe cleanup if it does not touch repositories, worktrees, artifacts, secrets, databases, model weights, user data, or dirty project state. If access is blocked, return a structured blocker and exact next access/failover step. Do not run on Mac.
allowed_safe_cleanup: journalctl --vacuum-time=7d or --vacuum-size=500M after recording journal size
apt-get clean after recording apt cache size
remove temp files older than 7 days from /tmp and /var/tmp only
docker builder prune for unused build cache only if docker system df shows build cache pressure
truncate or rotate oversized non-secret logs only after recording path and size
forbidden_cleanup: delete git repositories or dirty worktrees
delete model weights, embeddings, RAG indexes, or uploaded knowledge files
delete secrets, env files, SSH keys, tokens, cookies, or credentials
docker system prune -a or volume prune without explicit owner approval
systemctl restart unless explicitly approved by owner
package upgrades or service restarts unless required for artifact-safe cleanup
acceptance: qjns and uiap disk usage is classified with evidence.
No repositories, worktrees, artifacts, databases, model weights, RAG indexes, or user data are deleted.
If safe cleanup is performed, before/after df output proves reclaimed disk.
If cleanup cannot be performed, result is blocked with exact reason such as access_denied or no_safe_cleanup_candidate.
Control Plane node cards are rechecked after repair or blocker.
Before and after Control Plane node cards are recorded for each target.
Each target is handled one at a time; stop on unsafe signal.
Remote result reports task_id, node, Russian agent display name, target nodes, actions, verification, blockers, artifact paths, and next action.
